verdict.rationale: Circle's Wallets docs say developers get APIs to create wallets, sign transactions, and authorize actions through REST APIs or Web/Mobile SDKs. They also state the custody model: you don't manage raw private keys, and Circle secures keys with MPC or passkeys depending on the wallet product. The CLI also supports creating and managing wallets. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of per-customer or per-purpose wallet provisioning patterns, deposit address generation, in-depth custody documentation beyond the one-line MPC/passkey summary, and independent hands-on corroboration.
